title.en: Concentration of the filtrate and regulation of kidney function
title.kn: ಸೋಸಿದ ದ್ರವದ ಸಾಂದ್ರೀಕರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂತ್ರಪಿಂಡದ ಕಾರ್ಯ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ

hook.en: On a hot day in Raichur your urine is dark and little; after drinking lots of water it is pale and plenty. Something tells the kidneys how much water to keep.
hook.kn: ರಾಯಚೂರಿನ ಬಿಸಿಲಿನ ದಿನ ಮೂತ್ರ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮತ್ತು ಗಾಢ ಬಣ್ಣ; ಹೆಚ್ಚು ನೀರು ಕುಡಿದ ನಂತರ ತಿಳಿಯಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಎಷ್ಟು ನೀರು ಉಳಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ಮೂತ್ರಪಿಂಡಗಳಿಗೆ ಯಾರೋ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾರೆ.

objectives.en: Describe the roles of ADH, the RAAS and ANF

narration.en: On a hot day in Raichur your urine is dark and little; after drinking lots of water it is pale and plenty. Something tells the kidneys how much water to keep.
narration.kn: ರಾಯಚೂರಿನ ಬಿಸಿಲಿನ ದಿನ ಮೂತ್ರ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮತ್ತು ಗಾಢ ಬಣ್ಣ; ಹೆಚ್ಚು ನೀರು ಕುಡಿದ ನಂತರ ತಿಳಿಯಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಎಷ್ಟು ನೀರು ಉಳಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ಮೂತ್ರಪಿಂಡಗಳಿಗೆ ಯಾರೋ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾರೆ.

body.en: Mammals can produce concentrated urine. Henle's loop and the vasa recta play the major role. Filtrate flows in opposite directions in the two limbs of Henle's loop, and blood flows in opposite directions in the two limbs of the vasa recta: a counter-current. Together with the collecting duct, this keeps the osmolarity of the interstitium increasing from 300 mOsmol/L in the cortex to about 1200 mOsmol/L in the inner medulla. The gradient is mainly due to NaCl and urea: NaCl is transported by the ascending limb and exchanged with the descending limb of the vasa recta, and small amounts of urea enter the thin ascending limb and are returned to the interstitium by the collecting duct. Water then leaves the collecting duct easily, and human kidneys can make urine nearly four times as concentrated as the initial filtrate.
body.kn: ಹೆನ್ಲೆಯ ಕುಣಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ವಾಸಾ ರೆಕ್ಟಾದಲ್ಲಿ ದ್ರವ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಹರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ — ಇದೇ ಪ್ರತಿಪ್ರವಾಹ ಕ್ರಿಯಾವಿಧಾನ. ಅಂತರಾಳದ ಆಸ್ಮೊಲಾರಿಟಿ ಕಾರ್ಟೆಕ್ಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ 300 ರಿಂದ ಒಳ ಮೆಡುಲ್ಲಾದಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಮಾರು 1200 mOsmol/L ವರೆಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದಕ್ಕೆ NaCl ಮತ್ತು ಯೂರಿಯಾ ಕಾರಣ. ಮೂತ್ರ ಸುಮಾರು ನಾಲ್ಕು ಪಟ್ಟು ಸಾಂದ್ರವಾಗಬಹುದು.

points.en: 300 → 1200 mOsmol/L from cortex to inner medulla
Gradient made by NaCl and urea
Urine up to ~4 times as concentrated as the filtrate

body.en: Osmoreceptors in the body are activated by changes in blood volume, body fluid volume and ionic concentration. An excessive loss of fluid activates them to stimulate the hypothalamus to release antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or vasopressin from the neurohypophysis. ADH increases water reabsorption from the later parts of the tubule, preventing diuresis; it also constricts blood vessels, raising blood pressure and GFR. A fall in glomerular blood flow, blood pressure or GFR activates the JG cells to release renin, which converts angiotensinogen in blood to angiotensin I and then to angiotensin II. Angiotensin II, a powerful vasoconstrictor, raises glomerular blood pressure and GFR and makes the adrenal cortex release aldosterone, which causes reabsorption of Na+ and water from the distal parts of the tubule. This is the renin–angiotensin mechanism. An increase in blood flow to the atria makes them release atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which causes vasodilation, decreases blood pressure and acts as a check on the renin–angiotensin mechanism.
body.kn: ದ್ರವ ನಷ್ಟವಾದಾಗ ಹೈಪೋಥಲಾಮಸ್ ADH (ವ್ಯಾಸೋಪ್ರೆಸಿನ್) ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಅದು ನೀರಿನ ಮರುಹೀರಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. GFR ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದಾಗ JG ಕೋಶಗಳು ರೆನಿನ್ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ; ಆಂಜಿಯೋಟೆನ್ಸಿನ್ II ಮತ್ತು ಅಲ್ಡೋಸ್ಟೀರಾನ್ Na+ ಮತ್ತು ನೀರು ಉಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ANF ರಕ್ತದೊತ್ತಡವನ್ನು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ ಈ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಯನ್ನು ತಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Renin → angiotensin I → angiotensin II → aldosterone

problem.en: A student sweats heavily during a match and drinks no water. Predict the hormonal response and its effect on urine.

steps.en: Loss of body fluid raises the osmolarity of blood and lowers blood volume.
Osmoreceptors stimulate the hypothalamus; ADH is released from the neurohypophysis and increases water reabsorption from the DCT and collecting duct.
If blood pressure and GFR also fall, JG cells release renin; angiotensin II and aldosterone increase Na+ and water reabsorption.
Result: a small volume of concentrated urine.

answer.en: ADH and the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone mechanism make the kidneys save water, producing scanty, concentrated urine

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A student sweats heavily during a match and drinks no water. Predict the hormonal response and its effect on urine.

body.en: Diuresis means lots of urine. Anti-diuretic hormone stops it: more ADH → less, darker urine. ANF does the opposite of the renin–angiotensin chain: it widens vessels and lowers pressure.

narration.en: ADH = Anti-Diuretic = Hold the water. Diuresis means lots of urine. Anti-diuretic hormone stops it: more ADH → less, darker urine. ANF does the opposite of the renin–angiotensin chain: it widens vessels and lowers pressure.
